reference.title: Metrics from the design
reference.shortdesc: What each metric on the generate page counts, how it is obtained, and what the design aims for.

section.p: The two packs are measured together. A measured number comes from this run. A modeled number appears in the design only. Not in the MVP means the capability isn't built into this page.

strow.stentry: Requirements covered, current and approved
Requirements, across both packs, that have evidence, whose evidence topics are current for the model version, and whose last change was approved in Git.
100%, or a recorded decision for each gap
Measured
Evidence items with a named human approver from Git
Evidence items whose last commit merged through a pull request approved by a code owner who isn't the author or an agent.
Measured
Values in the packs that resolve from a key
Key references that resolve, checked by check_consistency.
Measured
Authority content found in downstream output

Matches for authority-only topic ids, titles and key values in the built downstream HTML. The same search runs on the authority pack as a control, so a result of 0 means the search can see the content.
Measured
Time from request to a pack ready for release
Seconds for the checks and both pack builds on the server. A person still has to review the findings.
Under 1 working day
Measured
People hours per pack
Not measured. The design models under 4 hours against 32 by hand.
Under 4
Modeled
Packs sealed with a locked policy and a manifest hash
Packs here carry a manifest hash but are never sealed. Sealing needs a human release and a locked bucket.
Not in the MVP

dlentry.dd: The measured value reaches the design target.
The value is short of the target. The row's note says why, for example gaps with no recorded decision.
The value is worse than allowed. For the leak metric, any match is a failure.
